title: Oxygen therapy
what: You breathe air with extra oxygen through small tubes in your nose or a mask. This raises the oxygen in your blood.
why: When your blood oxygen is low: with pneumonia, lung or heart disease, or after surgery. Sometimes oxygen is also prescribed for home.
duration: from a few hours to constant use, as your doctor decides
tell_doctor: If you smoke. No smoking near oxygen
If your nose gets dry or your ears hurt from the tubes

prepare.title: Safety
prepare.text: Oxygen makes fire burn stronger. No smoking, candles, or gas flames nearby, and no greasy creams on your face.

prepare.title: Flow rate
prepare.text: Your doctor decides how much oxygen to give. Do not change the flow yourself.

bring: A water-based lip balm. Your nose and lips may get dry
steps: The nurse chooses the nasal tubes or a mask
The tubes go into your nose and loop behind your ears
The oxygen is turned on at the flow your doctor prescribed
A sensor is clipped on your finger. It shows your oxygen level
Breathe as usual, through your nose or mouth
feel: A light flow of air in your nose
Your nose and mouth may get dry
The tubes sometimes rub behind your ears
after: Your oxygen level is checked regularly
The flow is lowered step by step as you get better
If oxygen is prescribed for home, you will be shown how to use the device
red_flags: Shortness of breath gets worse, blue lips, confusion, or strong drowsiness: call emergency services
At home, the device stops working and you feel unwell without oxygen: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I get addicted to oxygen?
faq.a: No, there is no addiction. Oxygen is given for as long as your body needs it.

faq.q: Can I eat and talk with tubes in my nose?
faq.a: Yes. Nasal tubes do not get in the way.

reminders.text: Check your oxygen: flow as your doctor set, and no fire or cigarettes nearby.
